Fred,

I'm in LA from tomorrow for Dentsu and the Griffin AGM, so can you take over the vendor and partner backlog this week? That's anyone outside the investor work who has an offer, a trial, a quote, terms or an ask in front of us and that one of us has actually engaged with: a call, a reply, a sign-up or paper. Cold pitches nobody answered, including ones we only forwarded around internally, stay off it, and so do the ad networks, PlayableX, Craftsman+ and Singular (they all stay on the UA budget call), the investors, and Mattel, which I'm keeping.

Go by the runway guardrails doc for what we do with each one, plus the one change I posted in #executives on Monday. Anything that needs signing goes the way ESG's note about signing says.

Everyone who is waiting to hear from us should get a written answer this week. Get each company's contact into Contacts so we're not digging through mail next time.

Log it all in a sheet in the Q4 commitments folder, the README in the folder has the columns. Then reply here with what we're keeping and what's waiting on Arthur or me to sign.

Thanks,
Leonard
======
Hi Leonard,

Following up on our call today, here's how we'd like agreements handled from now on while you're raising:

- Only an officer, you or Arthur, accepts terms or signs for Harmony Games, whatever the amount. That includes click-through terms and portal NDAs.
- Anything with an automatic renewal, exclusivity, a licence of your IP or a term over 12 months comes to us before anyone signs. Send each one to our intake address (it's in your Contacts as ESG Law intake), one email per agreement, so we can open a matter for it.
- Mutual NDAs on our template don't need review, whatever their term. An officer can sign them.

Best,
PERSON_2694_NAME
PARTNER, ESG Law
======
Agreed. This replaces what I said in July about Fred signing small stuff himself.

Fred, Arthur: anything waiting on Arthur or me to sign, put it on our founders' board To Do list with the company's name in the card title, including the ones that go to ESG. For the intake emails, what to include is in the intake checklist I shared.

Leonard
======

{"documentId": "f_b98287f6f80fe431a71209", "title": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments", "name": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments", "revisionId": "0d3b4ff7c7", "createdTime": "2025-09-26T16:00:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-26T18:00:00Z", "text": "Runway guardrails - Q4 commitments
Leonard, Sep 26. Until we know where the raise lands, this is how we handle anything outside the investor work that wants money, a signature or an answer from us.
How to decide
Go top to bottom and stop at the first one that fits.
1. Already answered. If one of us has already given them an answer, don't write to them again. Note who answered and when. If the answer was "later", it comes back at the January commitments review I'll put on our calendars too.
2. Cash test. Anything that would cost us cash between Oct 1 and Dec 31 ends now: say no, or cancel it in writing the way their paper or notice asks. A trial or pilot that turns into a paid plan inside that window counts as cash, and so does an offer we would have to take up and pay for before January. Travel and event costs count only when we book them ourselves.
3. Keep. The cash test has one exception: anything on Arthur's keep-running list on our board stays, even if it costs money. Tell them we're staying.
4. Sign. If it costs nothing before January but taking it means someone has to accept terms or sign for the company, it goes the way ESG's note says. Tell them it's with Leonard or Arthur to sign, and with our lawyers first when ESG has to see it.
5. Park. Everything else that's free until January, including offers we could still take up after that. Tell them we'll pick it up in January; it comes back at the January commitments review I'll put on our calendars (first week of January).
Answers
Everyone who is waiting to hear from us gets a written answer. Portals and no-reply notices don't need one.
"}

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

values: Quote: 12 rigged monster models, $6,400 (50% on kickoff)
Arthur passed: we're keeping the art in-house (no new message sent)
Creative retainer proposal, $3,500/month from Oct 1, 3-month minimum; asked us to confirm by Oct 1
No: not going ahead with the retainer, please don't book the team for October
ASO retainer proposal, $900/month from Oct 1 (3-month start); asked us to confirm by Oct 1
No: not going ahead with the ASO retainer, no need to send the contract
Store listing localization quote (12 languages), $2,640 invoiced on delivery; price holds until Oct 3; waiting on a PO
No: not placing the PO, let the quote lapse
Moderated player panel Oct 14, $1,200 prepaid; confirm by Oct 6
No: not booking the Oct 14 panel, don't recruit for us
Booth hold, Bay Area Indie Showcase Oct 24: $4,800, $2,400 deposit due Oct 10 (Fred said in June he'd come back to them)
No: release the booth hold, we won't pay the deposit
UGC Studio pilot hit its 20-video cap; pilot ends Oct 15 and the Studio plan ($1,800/month) starts Oct 16 unless cancelled in writing to billing@paylane.io by Oct 15
Cancelled the Studio plan in writing to billing@paylane.io (per the Paylane notice) and told Priya we're not carrying on after the pilot, no next brief
Trailer music pack annual licence, $1,188 paid on signature; quote holds until Oct 15
No: not taking the licence, no need to send it for signature
Pro order form: 4 seats, $149/month billed from Nov 1; asked for an answer by mid-October
No: not upgrading to Pro, please don't set it up
Seattle Indie Expo pre-registration push Nov 7: we'd pay travel and hotel for two, booked by Wishwave and invoiced at cost (~$1,600); confirm by Oct 17
No: not taking part, please don't book any travel for us
30-day trial (from Sep 19) moves to Growth at $79/month on Oct 20 unless cancelled by Oct 19; offered a walkthrough
Cancelled in writing to Hana (onboarding contact): please cancel before the trial ends, no paid plan; no walkthrough needed
November creator campaign, $8,000 with 50% deposit on booking; bookings close Oct 31
No: not booking the November slot
Indie showcase slot Dec 5, $750 stand fee (call with Robert Sep 17)
No: not taking the Dec 5 showcase slot
Nightly DB backups move to Standard, $19/month, renews Oct 12 (on Arthur's keep-running list)
Yes: keep the backups running on Standard from Oct 12
SSL certificate for the game API domain, $89/year, renewal due Oct 20 (keep-running list)
Yes: please renew and reissue before Oct 20
On-call paging (Arthur's night pager): Starter ends Oct 31, Team $29/month from Nov 1 under existing agreement
Mutual NDA on ESG's template (2-year term) before the Oct 8 call; officer signature needed
It's with Leonard to sign (ESG template, no review needed)
Publishing LOI for Zombie Match 3D in Japan/Korea, revenue share, 12-month exclusivity; signature by Oct 20
With our lawyers first, then Leonard to sign; sent to ESG intake
November puzzle week featuring agreement, no fees; accept in partner portal by an authorised signatory by Oct 24
It's with Leonard to accept in the portal
Startup Program agreement: $25k credits, 36-month term; sign by Oct 31 (cohort closes)
With our lawyers first, then Arthur to sign; sent to ESG intake
Holiday puzzle bundle participation agreement: no cost, rev share, 18-month licence of Domino Delights name/logo/art; sign by Nov 1
With our lawyers first, then Leonard to sign; sent to ESG intake
Southeast Asia publishing proposal for Domino Delights: 70/30 rev share, no upfront fee, 2-year exclusive term (Fred replied Sep 10 'we'll take a look')
With our lawyers first, then Leonard to sign; sent to ESG intake
Free brand-monitoring tier; click-through terms must be accepted in the dashboard
It's with Arthur to accept the terms; keep the setup on hold until then
App embedding licence for two display fonts, $640 when ordered; quote valid until Jan 31, 2026
We'll pick it up in January
Beta free through Jan 31, 2026, paid plans from February; asked for a 30-min feedback call
We'll pick it up in January (no feedback call for now)
Team trial free until Feb 1, 2026 ($8/user/month after); offered to add the rest of the team
We'll pick it up in January; don't add anyone for now
Trailer voice-over quote, $950 paid when a session is booked; valid until Feb 28, 2026
We'll pick it up in January
Full benchmark set subscription, $300/month from February 2026 (sample report free)
We'll pick it up in January
Free pilot slot in February 2026 for the website demo widget; asked whether to hold it
We'll pick it up in January
Pro upgrade proposal, $49/month from the day we upgrade; free plan continues
Staying on the free plan; we'll pick up Pro in January
Startup trial free until Jan 12, 2026, then Growth $99/month unless cancelled before Jan 12; asked if we'll stay on
We'll decide in January, before the trial ends
$10,000 credits reserved until Feb 28, 2026; asked whether to activate now or later
Later: we'll pick it up in January
Launch package for the 2026 release, $1,200 paid when booked, book any time before launch
We'll pick it up in January

input.subject: New agreement for review: Kinetic Arcade - publishing LOI (Harmony Games)
input.body:
Hi,

Please open a matter for this agreement.

- Company and agreement: Kinetic Arcade, letter of intent to publish Zombie Match 3D in Japan and Korea
- Term and renewal: 12 months from signature; no automatic renewal stated in the LOI
- Exclusivity / IP licence: exclusive for Japan and Korea for 12 months from signature; publishing implies a licence of our game in those territories
- Cost to us: none (revenue share, no fees to Harmony Games)
- Needed by: Oct 20, 2025
- Signer: Leonard Hayes

The LOI is attached on Noor Haddad's email of Sep 10 and I can forward it on request.

Thanks,
Frederick Stone
Harmony Games

input.subject: Cancellation - workspace HG-2291 (UGC Studio) - Harmony Games
input.body:
Hello,

Harmony Games is cancelling the UGC Studio Studio plan on workspace HG-2291 before it starts. Per your notice of Sep 12, the pilot ends on Oct 15, 2025; please do not start the Studio plan ($1,800/month) on Oct 16 and do not bill us for it.

Please confirm the cancellation in writing.

Frederick Stone
Harmony Games

Leonard,

The backlog is done. I went through it with the guardrails doc and your #executives change (partner-booked travel counts as cash). Every company waiting on us has a written answer. Their contacts are in Contacts, and the log is in the Q4 commitments folder as "Q4 commitments log" (33 companies): https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e147e61b0e0682e3/edit

WHAT WE'RE KEEPING (Arthur's keep-running list)
- Vaultline: nightly DB backups, $19/month Standard from the Oct 12 renewal
- Certwell: API domain SSL, $89/year, renewal due Oct 20
- Pingwise: the night pager. Team plan is $29/month from Nov 1; I told them not to downgrade us

WAITING ON YOU OR ARTHUR TO SIGN (all cards are on the To Do list on our Harmony Games board)
With ESG first. I sent one intake email per agreement today:
- Kinetic Arcade: Japan/Korea publishing LOI with 12-month exclusivity. You sign, by Oct 20
- Lumencloud: Startup Program agreement ($25k credits, 36-month term). Arthur signs, by Oct 31
- Bundlehouse: holiday bundle participation agreement (18-month licence of Domino Delights' name and art). You sign, by Nov 1
- Lanternfly Publishing: Southeast Asia publishing for Domino Delights (2-year exclusive). You sign; no deadline, they want it for their Q4 slate
No ESG review needed:
- Playfuse: mutual NDA on ESG's template. You sign, by Oct 8 (before their call)
- Orbit Store: November featuring agreement, no fees. You accept it in their partner portal, by Oct 24
- Markward: free brand-monitoring tier. Arthur accepts the click-through terms in their dashboard; no deadline

For the rest:
- Ended (said no or cancelled in writing): Brightlane, Ascendo, Lingora, Panelpulse, Pixel Harbor, Clipforge, Soundvault, Framewell, Wishwave, Reviewly, Streamcast, Spotlight Fest.
  - Clipforge: their pilot hit its video cap, so it would have turned into $1,800/month on Oct 16. I cancelled in writing to billing@paylane.io.
  - Reviewly would have gone to $79/month on Oct 20; Hana has the cancellation.
- Parked to the Jan 5 review: Glyphworks, Quillcraft, Loopnote, Driftwood Audio, Benchmarkly, Tilecast, Echohall, Retainly, Cloudlark, Pressbeam. There's a reminder for each on my calendar that day.
  - Retainly turns into $99/month on Jan 12 unless we cancel.
- Motive Forge: Arthur had already turned them down on Sep 19.

Fred

I've worked through the whole backlog and replied to Leonard on his email with what we're keeping and what's waiting on him or Arthur to sign. I followed his runway guardrails doc and the change he posted in #executives on Monday: travel a partner books and bills us for now counts as cash.

**What I decided for each of the 33 companies:**
- **Keep (3), from Arthur's keep-running list:**
  - Vaultline (nightly database backups): $19/month from Oct 12.
  - Certwell (SSL certificate for the game's API): $89, due Oct 20.
  - Pingwise (the night pager): $29/month from Nov 1.
- **Sign (7):** all on the To Do list of the Harmony Games board, with the company in each card title.
  - Four went to ESG first, one intake email each: Kinetic Arcade (by Oct 20), Lumencloud (by Oct 31), Bundlehouse (by Nov 1) and Lanternfly (no deadline).
  - Three need only an officer's signature: Playfuse NDA (by Oct 8), Orbit Store (by Oct 24) and Markward.
- **End (12):** each told no in writing, which closes off about $26k in Q4 spend.
  - Clipforge's pilot hit its video cap, so it would have become $1,800/month on Oct 16. I cancelled in writing to billing@paylane.io, as their notice asks.
  - Reviewly would have moved to $79/month on Oct 20. I asked Hana, our contact there, to cancel it.
- **Park (10):** each told we'll pick it up in January. Each has its own all-day reminder on your calendar for Jan 5, the day of the January review. Retainly becomes $99/month on Jan 12 unless we cancel.
- **Already answered (1):** Arthur turned down Motive Forge on Sep 19, so I didn't write to them.

Every company that was waiting on us has a written answer (32 replies). I added the 30 contacts that were missing, with the company in the job field. The log is "Q4 commitments log" in your Q4 commitments folder, shared with Leonard.

**Judgment calls you may want to check:**
- **Holding replies treated as unanswered:** you'd told Lanternfly "we'll take a look and get back to you" and Pixel Harbor "I'll come back to you". Both were still waiting, so I didn't count those as answers. Pixel Harbor gets a no before the $2,400 deposit due Oct 10. Lanternfly goes to signing.
- **Who signs:** I put Leonard on the publishing and partner deals, and Arthur on Lumencloud and Markward. That's easy to swap on the cards if you'd rather split it differently.
- **Left off the list:** Nova Rewards (withdrew its offer and nobody replied), Rayking (cold pitch only forwarded internally), the a16z thread (investor) and a design-recruiting pitch. None of them meet Leonard's bar.
- **Spotlight Fest:** gave no deadline, so its next date in the log is the Dec 5 event itself.
